n: The father opens his final warning about immorality by urging his son to treasure his teachings.
Guard these teachings as carefully as you protect the pupil of your eye—the most sensitive and precious part.

f.g: The pupil of the eye; something guarded instinctively and with great care.

n: Tie them on your fingers as a reminder and write them on your heart. The outward reminder and the inward commitment go together.
Make wisdom your sister and understanding your close relative. If wisdom is your family, you won’t be drawn to the false intimacy of the seductress.

f.g: kinswoman = female relative; close family member.

n: Wisdom’s purpose is protection from the smooth-talking adulteress.
The father tells a story like a parable, as if he watched it happen from his window.

f.g: casement = window lattice, a latticed opening.

n: He sees a naive young man among a group of youths, one lacking sense.
The young man wanders near her corner and heads toward her house. He isn’t forced; he drifts into temptation’s neighborhood.
Time passes from dusk to deep night. Darkness suggests both the hour and the moral setting.

f.w: in the black and dark night

n: A woman meets him dressed like a prostitute, with a cunning, guarded heart.

f.g: subtil = crafty, cunning; her heart is guarded and scheming.

n: An aside describes her: loud, defiant, restless—she never stays at home.
She is always out—in the streets, in the squares—waiting at every corner. Temptation actively hunts.
She grabs him, kisses him, and speaks with a brazen face.
She cloaks sin in religion: she has offered peace offerings and has meat from the sacrifice at home. Peace-offering meat had to be eaten quickly, giving her a reason to invite him to a feast.

f.g: Sacrifices whose meat was shared and eaten by the worshipper within a day or two.

n: She flatters him: she came out looking specifically for him. He is made to feel chosen and special.

f.g: Eagerly looking for you in particular.

n: She describes her luxurious bed covered with expensive imported fabrics from Egypt.

f.g: Egyptian linen was a prized luxury import.

n: She has scented it with exotic perfumes. Every detail appeals to the senses.
Her invitation is blunt: let’s indulge ourselves all night.
She assures him there’s no risk—her husband is away on a long trip.

f.g: goodman = the man of the house, the husband.

n: He took money and won’t be back until a set time, like the full moon. She promises secrecy and safety—both false.

f.g: Possibly “the day of the full moon,” a set date.

n: Her flood of persuasive words wins him over. Flattery can overpower a weak will.

f.g: She pushed or compelled him—overpowered his resistance.

n: He follows her at once, like an ox led to slaughter or a fool to punishment. He has no idea what awaits.

f.g: A device for restraining a prisoner; the Hebrew here is difficult.

n: He rushes like a bird into a trap, not knowing it will cost him his life—until an arrow pierces his vitals.

f.w: a dart strike through his liver
f.g: dart = arrow; the liver stood for the vital center of life.

n: The father turns from the story to apply it: children, listen carefully.
Don’t let your heart drift toward her ways, and don’t wander onto her paths.
She has brought down many victims, even strong men. No one is too strong to fall to this temptation.

f.w: many strong men have been slain by her

n: The sobering ending: her house is a highway to the grave, down into the rooms of death.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol—the grave, the place of the dead.
